newsitem.title: USA: Dominican president criticizes US immigration law.
newsitem.headline: Dominican president criticizes US immigration law.

text.p: The new Dominican president, who grew up in New York and attended the city's public schools, said recent U.S. legislation to tighten immigration could have a serious impact on his country.
Dominican Republic President Leonel Fernandez said U.S. laws making immigration more difficult would hurt the Dominican Republic's economy and could spark illegal immigration to the United States.
"One of the major pillars of the Dominican economy is the remittances of Dominicans' living abroad, especially in the New York area," Fernandez said.
The U.S. Congress approved legislation this week to overhaul immigration law.
"We need to make the Congress more aware of the impact this legislation has on countries like the Dominican Republic," Fernandez said.
If fewer Dominicans are able to send money home and economic conditions worsen in the Republic, many Dominicans could have no other possibility than trying to enter the United States illegally.
